body:
Pass 12. You resumed - ignore my pause note from last pass.

Prototyped your canonical-accumulation decision before Epic 5 builds it. It is achievable at 2x naive cost, not 27x. Across five workspace block plans: naive per-block crossprod is NOT bitwise identical (1.42e-13), a fixed canonical tile shape IS (max|diff| = 0, 2x cost), per-pair dot products also are but cost 27x.

The mechanism is the useful bit - the drift is BLAS switching kernels on matrix SHAPE, not your reduction order. So the rule for Epic 5 is: fix the GEMM tile shape, and let the workspace budget control tile COUNT only. Bucket supports into a small fixed set of canonical widths (powers of two over the Epic 1 support-size distribution) so padding waste stays bounded. Full numbers in the decision note on the bead.

Epic 4 looks good from pass 11 - both original defects fixed, verified. Still no commit though: 16 untracked R files.
